    Circular Poisson spatial scan statistic

    Source: R/spatial-scan.R
    epi_spatial_scan.Rd

    Scans circles centered on observed locations over user-specified radii. Under the null, cases are conditionally multinomial with probabilities proportional to population (a homogeneous Poisson risk). Candidate zones with population fraction exceeding max_fraction or containing no population outside are excluded. Only elevated-risk zones are considered. Reports the maximum conditional log likelihood ratio and a global Monte Carlo p-value based on the maximum over the same candidates in each null replicate, using (1 + number >= observed) / (nsim + 1). nsim=0 omits the p-value.

    Usage

    epi_spatial_scan(
  .data,
  x,
  y,
  cases,
  population,
  radii,
  max_fraction = 0.5,
  nsim = 199L
)

    Arguments

    .data

    Data frame of point locations or area centroids.

    x, y

    Numeric projected coordinates in the same units as radii.

    cases

    Non-negative integer case counts per location.

    population

    Positive population (or exposure) per location.

    radii

    Positive candidate radii in coordinate units.

    max_fraction

    Maximum fraction of population inside a candidate circle, strictly between zero and one.

    nsim

    Number of conditional Monte Carlo replicates; 0 omits testing.

    Value

    One-row tibble with the winning center, radius, inside counts and exposure, expected count, inside/outside relative risk, log likelihood ratio and global p-value. If all scores are zero the first candidate wins arbitrarily. Relative risk is infinite when outside cases are zero.

    Details

    Coordinates must be projected planar coordinates, not longitude/latitude. This basic spatial-only scan assumes cases and population belong to the same period and independent counts, with no confounder adjustment, temporal scan, age standardization, reporting bias correction or edge correction. Population is allocated to point locations, not polygons. Results depend on the candidate radii and centers; cluster selection and reported relative risk are subject to selection bias. A significant p-value is not proof of causation. Run set.seed() for reproducible simulation.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 10, 11), y = 0, cases = c(8, 7, 1, 1), pop = 100)
set.seed(1)
epi_spatial_scan(d, x, y, cases, pop, radii = c(0.1, 1), nsim = 19)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   center_x center_y radius observed expected population relative_risk
#>      <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1        0        0      1       15      8.5        200           7.5
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: log_likelihood_ratio <dbl>, p_value <dbl>,
#> #   simulations <int>, candidates <int>
